items.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Monk was very uh admiring of pianists, and I consider myself fortunate to be one of them. He was very nice to me all the time.

ctx.x: You've recorded a lot of Monk's music, visited Monk's music repeatedly in your repertoire.

Yeah, well Monk, Monk was very uh admiring of pianists, and I consider myself fortunate to be one of them. He was very nice to me all the time. You know, I mean, uh, we have no other person to uh, compare our relationship to, you know – except me and him. And he was always, you know, a piano player [pronounces "piano player" the way Monk always did]. He would say, he would talk with his teeth closed. He said, [imitating Monk], "piano players supposed to be sharp," he would say, for instance. And uh, uh another…
